question: Calculate the total revenue generated from all order items.
expected_sql: SELECT SUM(subtotal) AS total_revenue FROM order_items;

question: For each order, show the order id and total order amount, but only include orders with a total greater than 200.
expected_sql: SELECT order_id, SUM(subtotal) AS total_amount FROM order_items GROUP BY order_id HAVING SUM(subtotal) > 200;

question: Find customers who have placed more than one order and show how many orders each has placed.
expected_sql: SELECT c.customer_id, c.first_name, c.last_name, COUNT(o.order_id) AS order_count FROM customers c JOIN orders o ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id GROUP BY c.customer_id, c.first_name, c.last_name HAVING COUNT(o.order_id) > 1;

question: List all products that have never been ordered.
expected_sql: SELECT p.* FROM products p WHERE NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM order_items oi WHERE oi.product_id = p.product_id);

question: Find the top 3 most frequently ordered products by total quantity ordered.
expected_sql: SELECT p.product_name, SUM(oi.quantity) AS total_quantity FROM order_items oi JOIN products p ON oi.product_id = p.product_id GROUP BY p.product_name ORDER BY total_quantity DESC LIMIT 3;

question: For each customer, show the total amount they have spent, but only include customers who have spent more than 200 in total.
expected_sql: SELECT c.customer_id, c.first_name, c.last_name, SUM(oi.subtotal) AS total_spent FROM customers c JOIN orders o ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id JOIN order_items oi ON o.order_id = oi.order_id GROUP BY c.customer_id, c.first_name, c.last_name HAVING SUM(oi.subtotal) > 200;

question: List products that have at least two reviews and show their average rating.
expected_sql: SELECT p.product_name, COUNT(r.review_id) AS review_count, AVG(r.rating) AS avg_rating FROM products p JOIN reviews r ON p.product_id = r.product_id GROUP BY p.product_name HAVING COUNT(r.review_id) >= 2;

question: Find customers who have never placed any orders.
expected_sql: SELECT c.* FROM customers c LEFT JOIN orders o ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id WHERE o.order_id IS NULL;

question: For each product category, show how many products belong to that category.
expected_sql: SELECT category, COUNT(*) AS product_count FROM products GROUP BY category;

question: For each order, show the number of order items and the total quantity ordered, but only for orders with more than one item in total.
expected_sql: SELECT order_id, COUNT(*) AS line_count, SUM(quantity) AS total_quantity FROM order_items GROUP BY order_id HAVING SUM(quantity) > 1;

question: List all products in the 'Electronics' category that have at least one review with rating 5.
expected_sql: SELECT DISTINCT p.product_name FROM products p JOIN reviews r ON p.product_id = r.product_id WHERE p.category = 'Electronics' AND r.rating = 5;

question: Show all orders with their total order amount and status, ordered from highest to lowest total amount.
expected_sql: SELECT o.order_id, o.status, SUM(oi.subtotal) AS order_total FROM orders o JOIN order_items oi ON o.order_id = oi.order_id GROUP BY o.order_id, o.status ORDER BY order_total DESC;

question: For each product category, find the average price, but only include categories where the average price is greater than 100.
expected_sql: SELECT category, AVG(price) AS avg_price FROM products GROUP BY category HAVING AVG(price) > 100;

question: Find all customers who have ordered at least one product from the 'Home & Kitchen' category.
expected_sql: SELECT DISTINCT c.customer_id, c.first_name, c.last_name FROM customers c JOIN orders o ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id JOIN order_items oi ON o.order_id = oi.order_id JOIN products p ON oi.product_id = p.product_id WHERE p.category = 'Home & Kitchen';

question: List all products that have been ordered at least once but do not have any reviews.
expected_sql: SELECT DISTINCT p.product_name FROM products p WHERE EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM order_items oi WHERE oi.product_id = p.product_id) AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM reviews r WHERE r.product_id = p.product_id);

question: Show the earliest and latest order dates in the system.
expected_sql: SELECT MIN(order_date) AS earliest_order_date, MAX(order_date) AS latest_order_date FROM orders;

question: For each city, show how many customers live there, but only include cities with at least two customers.
expected_sql: SELECT city, COUNT(*) AS customer_count FROM customers GROUP BY city HAVING COUNT(*) >= 2;

question: List all customers who have written at least one review and show how many reviews each has written.
expected_sql: SELECT c.customer_id, c.first_name, c.last_name, COUNT(r.review_id) AS review_count FROM customers c JOIN reviews r ON c.customer_id = r.customer_id GROUP BY c.customer_id, c.first_name, c.last_name;

question: For each product category, show the total quantity of items ordered from that category.
expected_sql: SELECT p.category, SUM(oi.quantity) AS total_quantity FROM order_items oi JOIN products p ON oi.product_id = p.product_id GROUP BY p.category;

question: Find all orders that include at least one product from the 'Sports & Outdoors' category.
expected_sql: SELECT DISTINCT o.order_id, o.customer_id, o.status FROM orders o JOIN order_items oi ON o.order_id = oi.order_id JOIN products p ON oi.product_id = p.product_id WHERE p.category = 'Sports & Outdoors';

question: For each order status, calculate the total revenue from orders with that status.
expected_sql: SELECT o.status, SUM(oi.subtotal) AS total_revenue FROM orders o JOIN order_items oi ON o.order_id = oi.order_id GROUP BY o.status;

question: Find customers who have both placed at least one order and written at least one review.
expected_sql: SELECT DISTINCT c.customer_id, c.first_name, c.last_name FROM customers c JOIN orders o ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id JOIN reviews r ON c.customer_id = r.customer_id;

question: For each rating value, show how many reviews have that rating.
expected_sql: SELECT rating, COUNT(*) AS review_count FROM reviews GROUP BY rating;

question: List all products that have a stock quantity greater than 100 and that have been ordered at least once.
expected_sql: SELECT DISTINCT p.* FROM products p JOIN order_items oi ON p.product_id = oi.product_id WHERE p.stock_quantity > 100;

question: For each customer who has placed at least one order, show the date of their most recent order.
expected_sql: SELECT c.customer_id, c.first_name, c.last_name, MAX(o.order_date) AS latest_order_date FROM customers c JOIN orders o ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id GROUP BY c.customer_id, c.first_name, c.last_name;
